Review Bubble?

Reviewers largely see Bubble as a powerful way to build real web apps fast, especially for non-technical founders and MVPs, with strong support for workflows, databases, auth, plugins, and prototyping. Many say it can handle fairly complex products once you learn it. The main drawbacks are consistent: a steeper learning curve than advertised, sluggish performance compared with coded apps, clunky advanced API work, and weak mobile responsiveness that needs manual fixes. A few also mention scaling limits, an outdated interface, rotating IP issues, and frustrating subscription cancellation.

Bubble is a software development platform that enables anyone to build and launch web and mobile applications without writing code. Rather than specializing in one or two aspects of development (like designing landing pages or building databases), Bubble’s full-stack visual programming interface does it all. That means anyone from first-time founders to enterprises can take an idea from concept to fully functional, scalable reality — faster and cheaper than you could with just code.

#### What's great

Bubble lets you build a full web app with auth, database and workflows without writing code. For non-technical founders validating an idea, the speed from concept to live product is unmatched. The visual editor is powerful, the plugin ecosystem covers most integrations, and it's far cheaper than hiring a dev team for an MVP.

#### What needs improvement

Performance. Bubble apps feel sluggish compared to coded alternatives, especially on mobile. The learning curve is steeper than advertised. API integrations work but feel clunky beyond basic REST. Responsive design needs manual tweaking for every breakpoint. And once you hit serious traffic, you start fighting the platform instead of building on it.

#### vs Alternatives [...] #### vs Alternatives

Claude Code

Webflow for frontend-heavy sites, Adalo and FlutterFlow for mobile-first apps, Retool for internal tools. Bubble won on flexibility for complex logic and database relationships. The trade-off is that migrating to real code later means a full rebuild.

Nolan Vu

#### What's great

Bubble genuinely lets you build stuff that would normally require a full dev team. I used it to prototype a multi-step onboarding flow with a real backend, conditional logic, and user auth, and it actually held up. The visual workflow editor takes some getting used to but once it clicks, it's hard to go back.
